subtitle: Setting equity measures well means defining measures that are useful and explaining the reasoning behind proposed targets. You will also compare distributions honestly, without inventing a success that has not yet happened.
scope: For staff and leaders across DHS. Every person, request, queue, comparison and encounter is original example. Forty unique requests appear once in one shared exercise interval; the recorded event is a reply carrying a stated next step. North and South are invented processing labels, not actual demographic or eligibility groups. Target distributions use the same fixed hypothetical forty-request base and are not later observations, approvals or capacity plans. The garden encounter and Jules allegation example are distinct. Actual information and decision responsibilities, daily duties and qualifying formal analyses remain. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff carry their own equity work. Participation in this learning is voluntary. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters remain referral-only to the appropriate ADSA office.
introTranscript: Examine Morgan and Nina’s recorded reply baseline, proposed target and queue distributions. See how the same total can describe different allocations, and why a smaller gap is not the whole outcome. Hear personally offered meanings of progress, retain actual responsibilities and return a clear proposal with its open questions.

lessons.title: Begin with the question and the recorded event
lessons.summary: Read a baseline faithfully before treating a communication step as the result people need.
lessons.objective: Calculate the baseline for the complete practice request set.
objectives: Calculate the baseline for the complete practice request set.
Distinguish a reply carrying a stated next step from an understood or effective next step.
Explain how a changed denominator changes the question being answered.
takeaways: The event and base give a measure its meaning.
A recorded next step is not proof that the next step worked.
Changing the base can change the question rather than improve the result.
lessons.statement: A useful baseline describes what happened, to whom or what, and within which interval.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands while the third stands between them.

intro.heading: Begin with the question and the recorded event
intro.body:
Morgan and Nina are examining an original practice communication exercise across DHS work. Forty unique requests are counted once in one shared interval. Twenty-nine have a recorded reply carrying a stated next step during that interval; eleven do not have that event recorded within it. No actual applicant, employee, service record, eligibility decision or demographic category is supplied. The immediate purpose is to describe the recorded communication step and consider what a useful improvement would mean.

Twenty-nine divided by forty is 72.5 percent. The event is a reply with a stated next step recorded in the exercise interval. It is not receipt by the person, understanding, a correct instruction or resolution of the request. A message can contain a next step and still be unclear or unsuitable. The eleven other requests have no such event recorded in this interval. Earlier or later communication and unmet needs remain unknown; the exercise does not convert their absence here into proof that assistance never occurred.

Nina’s first draft calls 72.5 percent a successful service rate. Morgan asks where the exercise establishes successful service. The correction keeps the useful count but names its narrower event. A recorded communication step can matter to a process review while leaving the wider question of a usable next action unanswered. Making the statement precise is preferable to either declaring success or discarding all information because it is incomplete.

Morgan then considers reporting twenty-nine qualifying replies out of the twenty-nine requests that received those replies: 100 percent. The arithmetic is true for that altered base, but it answers a different question. It describes the selected reply set, not coverage across all forty requests. It cannot show that the original request-set proportion improved. Keep the forty-request base when comparing this defined event in this complete practice set. In actual work, a denominator must fit the specific question; this exercise does not require every measure to use all eligible people, every applicant or the same base.

A faithful baseline also states the interval and counting unit. Here, each invented request appears once. A live measure involving several messages, repeat requests or different observation periods would require its own clear definitions. The course gives no authority to obtain actual records or link people’s information to settle those definitions. Appropriate roles, purpose and information arrangements remain necessary outside the exercise.

Privately write one sentence with the event, twenty-nine-of-forty base and 72.5 percent result, followed by one unanswered experience question. For example, ask whether the stated next step was usable. This is valuable learning without a live case, publication, compulsory biography or personnel score. The baseline becomes more useful because its meaning is clear, not because it has been enlarged into an outcome the evidence does not establish.

accordion.heading: Examine the comparison and its consequences

items.title: Name the narrower event
items.body: Nina’s phrase successful service rate asks the twenty-nine replies to prove receipt, accuracy, understanding and resolved need. None is supplied. A more faithful sentence retains the communication event and its interval. The consequence is a usable starting comparison and a separate question about experience, rather than a service-success claim or the abandonment of an accurate count.

items.title: Keep the absent event at its actual scope
items.body: Eleven requests lack the recorded qualifying reply within the exercise interval. Nina can identify them as outside the numerator without declaring eleven people never received help. If a later event or an earlier contact matters to a new question, its evidence is not present here. The current count remains valid for its defined purpose; uncertainty about another event remains uncertainty.

items.title: Explain a changed base
items.body: Morgan’s twenty-nine-of-twenty-nine proposal yields 100 percent among a selected set already defined by the qualifying reply. That is not the original forty-request question. Using it as improvement would remove the eleven requests whose coverage prompted inquiry. A different actual question may legitimately need a different base, but its definition must be stated rather than presented as a like-for-like improvement.

tabs.heading: Compare the interpretation and the next consideration

tabs.label: A selected set becomes improvement
tabs.body: Morgan reports 100 percent because twenty-nine of the twenty-nine qualifying-reply requests had qualifying replies. The figure is a description of that selected set. It cannot be compared as an improvement over twenty-nine of all forty requests. The change in question hides the eleven requests without the interval event; the faithful response explains the selection before deciding whether that new question has a purpose.

tabs.label: The count becomes every outcome
tabs.body: Nina retains forty as the base but calls the twenty-nine events completed services. The base is consistent, yet the event’s meaning has changed without evidence. Receipt, understanding, correctness and resolved need could each require different information. The useful result is twenty-nine recorded replies carrying a stated next step, accompanied by an experience question, not an invented wider success rate.

tabs.label: The comparison retains its purpose
tabs.body: Morgan writes that twenty-nine of forty unique requests had a recorded reply carrying a stated next step in the shared interval, 72.5 percent. Nina keeps the other eleven visible and asks whether a stated next step was usable. The baseline describes its actual event and can support a later appropriately defined comparison. No answer to the experience question or later change is claimed.

check.question: Which statement describes the complete practice baseline?
check.correct: Twenty-nine of forty unique requests had a recorded reply carrying a stated next step in the interval, 72.5 percent; understanding and resolution remain unknown.
wrong: Twenty-nine replies establish twenty-nine successfully completed services.
Twenty-nine of the twenty-nine qualifying reply requests proves coverage improved to 100 percent.
The eleven other requests prove assistance never occurred.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The event, full exercise base and interval stay visible without an enlarged outcome.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A stated next step does not establish completed service. Selecting only qualifying replies changes the coverage question and supplies no later improvement. No interval event is not proof of no assistance at any time.

lessons.title: Give a target a reason and a clear status
lessons.summary: Separate a proposed improvement from an observed result, approved commitment or demonstrated capacity.
lessons.objective: Calculate what a proposed 90 percent target would mean for the same practice forty-request base.
objectives: Calculate what a proposed 90 percent target would mean for the same practice forty-request base.
Identify the reasons and evidence needed to consider a target in actual work.
Distinguish a planning illustration from approval, feasibility and a future result.
takeaways: A proposed target is a planning choice, not an observed event.
A target needs a purpose and a reason beyond an attractive number.
Capacity, authority and useful outcomes remain separate questions.
lessons.statement: Describe why a target is worth considering and what remains unestablished.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands while the third stands between them.

intro.heading: Give a target a reason and a clear status
intro.body:
Morgan and Nina next consider a planning illustration: a proposed 90 percent target for the same qualifying reply event and fixed hypothetical forty-request base. Ninety percent of forty is thirty-six. Compared with the twenty-nine recorded baseline events, that is seven more qualifying replies in the arithmetic. These are hypothetical comparison figures. There is no future observation, actual staffing plan, approved commitment, funding decision or demonstrated ability to deliver seven additional events.

Nina likes 90 percent because it is easy to remember. Morgan asks what makes it an appropriate target. Ease of communication can help readers follow a proposal, but it does not establish that the proposal fits the problem or can be delivered. The question is what change matters, whose experience is involved, what the selected event tells us and which other effects need examination. A target for a communication step may be useful while understanding and correct next action still require attention.

An actual proposal would need a reason informed by the relevant evidence and people affected. It could consider the starting condition, the importance of the missed step, uncertainty in the information, resources, constraints and possible unwanted effects. The exact evidence and responsible roles depend on the real issue. The course supplies no compulsory quota, universal improvement percentage or deadline. It also gives staff no authority to change eligibility, approve expenditures, assign another person’s work or declare that a number has leadership approval.

Morgan initially describes the additional seven events as seven people helped. Nina corrects the description: seven additional qualifying replies in this fixed-base illustration would raise the defined event from twenty-nine to thirty-six. Whether those replies were received, understandable, correct and useful remains unknown. An ambitious reply target might be worth considering, but speed or volume alone should not stand in for the result people need. The quality question should remain explicit rather than assumed from a larger numerator.

Keep baseline, target and later observation in separate sentences. The baseline is the supplied twenty-nine of forty, 72.5 percent. The target illustration is thirty-six of the same hypothetical forty, 90 percent. A later observed condition is not supplied. If actual periods later have different volumes or counting rules, their comparisons would need their definitions and limitations, not a practice fixed denominator imposed on real work.

Privately draft a short proposal describing the possible target, its purpose and what evidence is still needed to consider it. You can conclude that the reason is not yet adequate. That is a meaningful analytical result, not failed learning. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff carry their own equity work. Optional consultation helps thinking; it does not create a mandatory approval gate for every use of a resource or replace actual decision responsibilities.

accordion.heading: Examine the comparison and its consequences

items.title: Keep the three statuses distinct
items.body: Twenty-nine of forty is the supplied baseline event count. Thirty-six of the same hypothetical forty is a proposed target illustration. Neither provides a later observed result. If Nina says the target has been reached, a planning number has become invented evidence. Keeping the statuses separate allows a proposal to be discussed without implying that a change happened or was approved.

items.title: Ask what makes the target fitting
items.body: A memorable 90 percent is easy to state, but it supplies no reason for selecting that level. Morgan can ask why the event matters, how the current situation was understood, what affected people may need and what evidence could support a practical proposal. These questions can expose an inadequate rationale. They do not authorize new collection, funding or a universally required target.

items.title: Retain useful outcomes and constraints
items.body: Seven more qualifying replies in the illustration would improve the specified event count. They do not establish seven correct or understood next actions. A real proposal also needs to consider resources, responsibility and unwanted effects. Keeping these open prevents the attractive number from promising a usable service outcome or silently assigning delivery commitments that the practice exercise cannot approve.

tabs.heading: Compare the interpretation and the next consideration

tabs.label: The target becomes an achieved result
tabs.body: Nina writes that 90 percent now receive the needed help because thirty-six of forty is the proposed target. No later events are supplied, and even a recorded reply would not establish needed help. Morgan separates the supplied baseline from the hypothetical target and names the unresolved experience question. The proposal can still be examined; it cannot be reported as an observed improvement.

tabs.label: The arithmetic becomes capacity
tabs.body: Morgan concludes that only seven more replies are needed, so no additional effort or decision is necessary. The subtraction is correct, but it contains no information about actual work, constraints or quality. Nina retains seven as a hypothetical event difference and asks what evidence would help assess delivery and usefulness. Actual resource and operational responsibilities remain with their appropriate roles.

tabs.label: The proposal has a question and limits
tabs.body: Nina describes a possible 90 percent qualifying-reply target, equivalent to thirty-six of the same hypothetical forty, and identifies a need to examine its rationale, capacity and useful next action. The supplied baseline remains twenty-nine. The statement supports informed consideration without claiming approval, an arbitrary deadline, funding, a later result or a guaranteed benefit to seven people.

check.question: What does the proposed 90 percent illustration establish?
check.correct: Thirty-six qualifying replies out of the same hypothetical forty would be 90 percent, seven more than the baseline; rationale, capacity, approval and later results remain open.
wrong: Thirty-six actual people have now received useful help.
The simple seven-event difference proves current resources are sufficient.
Every DHS measure must reach 90 percent by the next review.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The planning arithmetic is retained without becoming an actual commitment or outcome.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The exercise supplies no later people’s results. Event subtraction does not assess capacity or usefulness. No universal target or deadline is provided.

items.text: Thirty-six of the same hypothetical forty is 90 percent.
Thirty-six minus twenty-nine is seven events.
Why is this target fitting for the actual issue?
What evidence would help assess capacity and useful next actions?
The target is an approved delivery commitment.
Seven more people have now had their needs resolved.

lessons.transfer: Privately write a proposed target, its purpose and the unanswered considerations; keep the baseline separate.

move.control: You can discuss a target without confusing planning, approval, capacity and achievement.
move.failure: An attractive number becomes a universal mandate or already observed success.

lessons.title: Look beneath the overall percentage
lessons.summary: Compare the same overall target with different distributions and preserve each recorded level.
lessons.objective: Calculate the two practice queue percentages and their baseline percentage-point gap.
objectives: Calculate the two practice queue percentages and their baseline percentage-point gap.
Compare two hypothetical distributions that reach the same overall 90 percent.
Explain why a smaller gap alone does not establish a useful result for everyone.
takeaways: An overall proportion can hide different recorded levels.
A reduced gap can coexist with a decline and does not by itself establish a meaningful outcome.
lessons.statement: Read the overall result, each relevant level and the gap together.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands while the third stands between them.

intro.heading: Look beneath the overall percentage
intro.body:
The same original forty-request baseline has two invented processing queues. North contains twenty unique requests, eighteen with the qualifying recorded reply. South contains twenty, eleven with that event. North is eighteen divided by twenty, 90 percent. South is eleven divided by twenty, 55 percent. The overall total remains twenty-nine of forty, 72.5 percent. The difference between 90 and 55 is thirty-five percentage points. These are processing labels in a wholly practice exercise, not demographic identities, service eligibility groups or actual DHS performance.

The difference identifies a question about this recorded event. It does not establish why the two queues differ, whether requests are otherwise comparable, what a person understood or whether a policy-defined disparity has been demonstrated. The numbers are intentionally simple to teach comparison. An actual inquiry would need the fitting evidence, context and responsible information arrangements rather than an invented explanation about need, effort or culture.

Morgan and Nina examine two hypothetical ways to distribute thirty-six qualifying replies across the same fixed forty requests. In the first illustration, North has twenty of twenty, 100 percent, and South sixteen of twenty, 80 percent. Together they have thirty-six of forty, 90 percent, with a twenty-percentage-point gap. Compared with the supplied baseline, this illustration adds two events in North and five in South.

In the second illustration, North has eighteen of twenty, 90 percent, and South eighteen of twenty, 90 percent. The total is again thirty-six of forty, 90 percent, but the gap is zero. North’s event count is unchanged from the baseline and South’s is seven higher. The equal overall target hides a different allocation. Neither illustration is observed future work, an approved resource plan or proof that replies would be understood and useful.

A third hypothetical distribution makes a different caution visible: sixteen of twenty in each queue. Both are 80 percent, the overall result is thirty-two of forty, 80 percent, and the gap is zero. Relative to the baseline, North’s recorded level falls ten percentage points and South’s rises twenty-five. The overall proportion rises seven and a half percentage points from 72.5 to 80. A zero gap alone does not communicate North’s decline, South’s increase or the unresolved quality question. Equality of this event is not the complete definition of success.

Privately compare all three illustrations by writing the overall proportion, each queue’s level and their percentage-point gap. Keep baseline and hypothetical status explicit. Ask what additional context and useful-outcome evidence would matter before recommending actual action. Staff can learn from this complete an example without identifying real people, changing a dashboard or treating every descriptive difference as a proven systemic cause. A sound comparison keeps the important question visible while remaining honest about what the figures do not answer.

accordion.heading: Examine the comparison and its consequences

items.title: Reconcile the baseline parts and whole
items.body: Eighteen North events plus eleven South events gives twenty-nine; twenty requests in each gives forty. The 90 and 55 percent levels therefore fit the overall 72.5 percent. Reading only the overall result loses the thirty-five-point difference. Reading only the gap loses each level. None of these accurate descriptions identifies a cause, useful next action or actual demographic outcome.

items.title: Compare two ways to reach thirty-six
items.body: Twenty North and sixteen South events yield 100 and 80 percent, a twenty-point gap. Eighteen in each yield 90 and 90, a zero gap. Both total thirty-six of forty. The difference is analytically important even though their overall target is identical. It still does not establish which distribution is feasible, whether the event benefits people or who has authority to implement a plan.

items.title: Notice a decline inside an equal result
items.body: Sixteen in each queue yields 80 percent overall and a zero gap. North falls from 90 to 80 while South rises from 55 to 80; the overall proportion rises from 72.5 to 80. Nina cannot call zero gap a complete shared success without describing these movements and the event’s limitations. Equal levels can matter, but they cannot erase a decline or substitute for evidence that the communication helped.

tabs.heading: Compare the interpretation and the next consideration

tabs.label: The same total hides allocation
tabs.body: Morgan groups both thirty-six-event illustrations under 90 percent and calls them identical. Nina writes out the twenty-and-sixteen allocation beside eighteen-and-eighteen. Their overall proportions match, but their queue levels and gaps differ. Retaining the distribution makes the comparison more informative. It does not supply actual capacity, cause, group characteristics or an approved preference for either hypothetical arrangement.

tabs.label: Zero gap becomes every benefit
tabs.body: Nina highlights sixteen events in each queue because both levels are equal. Morgan adds the baseline: North eighteen, South eleven. The equal illustration contains a North decline and South increase, with an overall increase of three events. Calling it success from the gap alone would omit that movement and the still-unanswered useful-next-action question. Describe levels, gap and purpose before proposing a conclusion.

tabs.label: The full comparison raises a fitting question
tabs.body: Morgan retains twenty-nine baseline events, the two thirty-six-event alternatives and the thirty-two-event equal illustration. Nina reports each queue’s percentage and the gap alongside the total. The next question concerns what context, capacity and useful-outcome evidence would support a real recommendation. The arithmetic illuminates options without proving the reason for a difference or turning a hypothetical distribution into a delivery plan.

lessons.title: Hear what progress means to another person
lessons.summary: Let personally offered meanings widen a judgment without making one measure everyone’s definition of commitment.
lessons.objective: Describe Leta’s and Hollis’s different personally chosen meanings of progress.
objectives: Describe Leta’s and Hollis’s different personally chosen meanings of progress.
Explain how Remy’s initial judgments change after hearing those meanings.
Develop an invitation that preserves a meaningful step and its interval without requiring personal disclosure.
takeaways: A visible step can carry different personal meanings.
A slower visible change is not proof of weak commitment.
A changed invitation can reflect understanding without proving agreement or a completed result.
lessons.statement: Ask what the marker of progress means before judging the person by it.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands while the third stands between them.

intro.heading: Hear what progress means to another person
intro.body:
In a separate conversation, Remy helps plan a progress display for a neighborhood garden gathering. This is not the DHS request exercise and supplies no actual event or completed display. Remy proposes a checklist of small completed steps because each visible mark seems to show commitment. Leta welcomes small marks; Hollis asks whether a meaningful interval of care can also be recognized. Remy initially hears Leta’s approach as busywork and Hollis’s approach as reluctance to show progress. Those are interpretations, not facts about the two people.

Leta offers a chosen experience from a weaving circle. Small milestones let a person see that repeated effort is contributing to a longer piece. Recognizing a completed step can encourage care and make an unfinished whole feel approachable. Leta is not asking for a person’s worth to be measured by a daily tick or for someone else’s biography. The meaning is a personally valued connection between a visible step and continued effort, not a rule about a cultural group.

Hollis offers a different chosen experience from tending seasonal plants with neighbors. Watering, observing and adjusting care can matter before a flower appears. An interval with little visible change need not mean no contribution. Hollis values explaining why the chosen interval fits the living process, rather than treating a slower visible result as a lack of commitment. This is a particular personal meaning, not evidence that all gardeners reject milestones or every long interval reflects effective care.

Remy’s understanding changes in two directions. Leta’s small markers are no longer dismissed as trivial activity; they can express recognizable effort toward a meaningful whole. Hollis’s interval is no longer read as avoidance; it can express sustained care whose visible result takes time. Neither account forces Remy to conclude that any tick is worthwhile or any absence of visible change is healthy. The accounts widen the initial judgment while preserving the need to explain what the step and interval actually show.

Remy revises the invitation: participants may suggest a meaningful garden step and explain a fitting interval for recognizing it, without providing a personal story. A small completed task could be recognized alongside an explanation that a different contribution requires continuing care. The revised offer does not announce acceptance, event success or a completed display. Leta and Hollis have meanings the people describe that change Remy’s offer; whether the proposal is used remains open.

Return privately to the distinction between a marker and its meaning. In the separate DHS arithmetic, a recorded reply can be a useful process step without establishing every useful outcome. That analytical caution can coexist with this personal learning, but the people’s meanings are not causes of the queue figures. No intercultural orientation, employee rating, demographic script or compulsory disclosure follows from the encounter. Understanding another person’s meaning can be worthwhile even before a public artifact or agreement is produced.

accordion.heading: Examine the comparison and its consequences

items.title: Hear Leta’s meaning without a daily quota
items.body: The weaving-circle account connects a small milestone to recognizable continued effort. Remy initially dismisses the marks as busywork, missing that meaning. A better response can ask what the proposed garden step contributes to the whole. It does not make every tick valuable, prescribe daily frequency or require anyone to demonstrate commitment through personal history. Leta’s meaning is individually offered and context-specific.

items.title: Hear Hollis’s meaning without excusing every absence
items.body: Seasonal care can contribute before a visible flower. Remy’s first interpretation equates a slower visible result with reluctance. Hollis’s account gives a reason to examine whether the chosen interval fits the process. It does not prove all delays are useful or all care effective. The changed understanding retains a meaningful question while avoiding a judgment about the person from one visible pattern.

items.title: Change the offer while keeping results open
items.body: Remy invites a meaningful step and a reason for its fitting interval without asking for biographies. This responds to both offered meanings. It does not require agreement, complete a display or establish a group trait. A clearer offer is itself a real change in the example, even though what participants choose and whether the event happens remain unknown.

tabs.heading: Compare the interpretation and the next consideration

tabs.label: One marker ranks commitment
tabs.body: Remy requires frequent checklist marks and reads slower visible change as disengagement. That interpretation misses Hollis’s personally offered meaning of continuing seasonal care and can also turn Leta’s milestone into a compulsory daily test. Neither account supports a ranking of people. Ask what the marker contributes and why the interval fits, while retaining actual responsibilities and the option not to share a personal story.

tabs.label: The milestone is dismissed
tabs.body: Remy removes all small-step recognition because it looks like busywork. Leta’s weaving-circle account explains how a milestone can connect effort to an unfinished whole. Remy can consider a meaningful step without asserting that every tick proves benefit. The change is understanding a chosen meaning rather than using a person’s narrative as proof that a particular display must be adopted.

tabs.label: The invitation reflects both meanings
tabs.body: Remy proposes meaningful steps with an explanation of their fitting intervals. That offer can make small contributions recognizable and allow sustained care to be understood before an immediate visible result. No participant is asked to supply a biography, and no completed display or agreement is claimed. The encounter supports widened understanding; it does not explain the practice queue gap or determine an IDI position.

check.question: What changed in the supplied garden encounter?
check.correct: Remy’s busywork and reluctance judgments widen, and the revised invitation welcomes meaningful steps with fitting intervals without requiring biographies; acceptance remains open.
wrong: Hollis’s account proves every delayed visible result is useful.
Leta’s meaning establishes a daily progress quota for everyone.
The garden accounts explain the thirty-five-point DHS queue gap.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The particular meanings change the interpretation and offer without inventing a wider result.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A chosen meaning of sustained care does not establish that all delays help. A meaningful milestone is not a compulsory frequency or biography test. The separate personal encounter provides no cause for the practice request figures.

sorting.heading: Keep evidence, proposals and outcomes distinct

items.text: Leta connects a small milestone to continued effort toward a whole.
Hollis connects a fitting interval to sustained seasonal care.
Remy’s initial busywork and reluctance judgments widen.
Remy revises the invitation without a biography requirement.
All participants accepted and completed the display.
The two accounts identify anyone’s IDI orientation.

lessons.title: Keep information and decision responsibilities intact
lessons.summary: A useful proposal does not provide new data access, operating authority or a substitute for required action.
lessons.objective: Distinguish a practice analytical proposal from authority to collect information or change actual work.
objectives: Distinguish a practice analytical proposal from authority to collect information or change actual work.
Identify information questions that an actual measure would need to address with its responsible roles.
Recognize the immediate manager reporting duty in the distinct protected-class allegation example.
takeaways: A question does not authorize every method for answering it.
A proposed target does not delegate spending or operating decisions.
Optional learning does not delay required reporting or assigned investigation.
lessons.statement: Keep the useful inquiry and the actual responsibilities together.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands while the third stands between them.

intro.heading: Keep information and decision responsibilities intact
intro.body:
Morgan and Nina’s original sample figures help examine a measure; they do not grant authority to retrieve actual records, create demographic categories, link people’s information or publish a new dashboard. North and South remain invented processing queues. The relevant next question is what evidence would help understand the communication step and its usefulness, not how to bypass the arrangements that govern information and actual decisions.

In real work, a proposed measure must fit its purpose and the evidence’s intended use. The current Minnesota data-practices provisions address necessity and limits on purposes for information about individuals, along with accuracy and access safeguards. The responsible arrangements must be followed for the actual information and activity. This course supplies neither a complete legal interpretation nor permission to collect, combine or disclose a person’s data. A lower count, a removed name or a consultant request is not an automatic certificate that a release is safe or authorized.

Morgan considers adding demographic fields to explain the invented queue gap. Nina asks what question each field would serve and what actual authority and information arrangements would apply. They do not collect new fields in the exercise. The gap is descriptive and does not reveal a demographic cause. A proposal can identify missing evidence without assuming that every potentially interesting detail should be gathered. Actual record access, reporting, collection and sharing stay with their responsible roles and procedures.

The same distinction applies to delivery. Nina can recommend considering whether clearer next-step communication is needed. That does not approve staffing, a new schedule, eligibility rules, procurement, expenditures or a change to actual service operations. Appropriate decisions and responsibilities remain. Staff develop and carry their own equity work with program guidance, knowledge and feedback from the Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant. Consultation supports capability; no universal consultant gate is added to use these resources.

A distinct example concerns supervisor Jules. During a measure-review conversation, Jules receives a disability-related harassment or discrimination allegation about how a colleague was treated. Managers and supervisors immediately report all protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer, and follow applicable agency complaint and investigation procedures or the Affirmative Action Plan. The allegation does not wait for a complete chart, verified proof, consensus, an apology, a course or consultant response. Assigned investigation and nonretaliation remain; this is not permission for an improvised substitute investigation.

That reporting example must stay distinct from the processing-queue arithmetic. A descriptive difference is not by itself the supplied protected-class allegation, and every unresolved measure question is not the same trigger. You can privately practice both distinctions without obtaining an actual record or personal account. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters remain referral-only to the appropriate ADSA office. Completion of this voluntary learning does not count toward DHS-required training credits unless management, a director or DHS leadership expressly approves an exception.

The intended use that helps determine what evidence is fitting and which actual arrangements apply.

accordion.heading: Examine the comparison and its consequences

items.title: A field needs a purpose and actual arrangements
items.body: Morgan wants demographic fields because a queue gap is visible. Nina asks what each field would answer and which actual responsibilities apply. No new information is collected. A missing-evidence statement can be useful without becoming unrestricted access or a demand for every personal characteristic. Neither the invented queue names nor the proposed target supplies a demographic cause, data permission or an actual release decision.

items.title: A recommendation does not assign delivery
items.body: Nina can propose considering a clearer next-step process while acknowledging that no actual service content, staffing or capacity plan is supplied. Morgan cannot convert that proposal into approved expenditure or another person’s assignment. The useful recommendation names what needs examination and keeps real decisions with their responsible roles. Consultant guidance builds staff capability without becoming a universal approval requirement.

items.title: A protected-class allegation has its own duty
items.body: Jules’s disability-related allegation triggers the immediate manager reporting requirement, not a wait for analytical certainty. Actual agency procedures and assigned investigation remain. A measure can be examined in parallel, but proof, a completed course, agreement or a consultant reply cannot become a condition for the report. This distinct example does not turn every numerical difference into the same allegation or authorize a separate informal investigation.

tabs.heading: Compare the interpretation and the next consideration

tabs.label: The chart grants access
tabs.body: Morgan treats the thirty-five-point queue gap as permission to open individual records and add every demographic field. The figures establish no such authority or cause. Nina retains the analytical question, specifies the missing evidence and follows actual information arrangements before any live activity. The private exercise can still be completed without personal records or a claim that removing names alone resolves disclosure questions.

tabs.label: The target grants delivery authority
tabs.body: Nina treats thirty-six hypothetical events as an approved staffing and service commitment. No capacity, expenditure or delegated operating decision is supplied. Morgan can instead label it a target illustration and identify what evidence and responsible decisions would matter. The proposal remains substantive, but its status is accurate and does not assign a real deadline or approve a service change.

tabs.label: The two triggers stay distinct
tabs.body: Morgan preserves the queue comparison as a recorded-event inquiry. In the separate Jules example, the protected-class allegation is reported immediately through the required manager route and actual procedures continue. Neither replaces the other. The distinction avoids both waiting for a finished analysis before reporting an allegation and treating an unanswered descriptive difference as proof of a protected-class cause.

check.question: What is the appropriate response in the distinct Jules example?
check.correct: Report the protected-class allegation immediately to HR or the agency AAO and follow applicable agency procedures or the Affirmative Action Plan; do not wait for the measure review.
wrong: Wait until the queue comparison proves the allegation.
Require the colleague to complete this course before the report.
Replace the required process with a private consultant discussion.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The reporting duty is distinct from optional analysis and learning; assigned investigation remains.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A completed numerical comparison is not a reporting condition. Course completion cannot delay the duty. Consultant guidance does not replace the required reporting process.

sorting.heading: Keep evidence, proposals and outcomes distinct

items.text: Jules’s immediate required report and applicable procedures.
Existing information and assigned decision arrangements.
Consider what evidence would help understand useful next actions.
Compare the two hypothetical thirty-six-event distributions.
Link actual personal records merely because the target looks helpful.
Approve expenditures by completing the course.

scenario.context: This example: Morgan proposes additional demographic fields after seeing the processing-queue gap. No actual fields, authority, records or collection decision are supplied.
scenario.prompt: Which response preserves a useful inquiry?
options: Collect every potentially interesting field without a stated purpose.
Name the question and missing evidence, keep the gap descriptive and follow actual information responsibilities before any live work.
Treat the processing labels as actual demographic categories.
responses: Potential interest alone does not supply the actual purpose and responsibilities.
The inquiry remains useful without turning uncertainty into permission or cause.
The queue names are invented processing labels, not demographic identities.

lessons.transfer: Privately separate a proposed inquiry, its unanswered information questions and actual responsibilities; keep the Jules allegation route distinct.

move.control: You can preserve a substantive measure proposal without granting unsupported authority or delaying required action.
move.failure: Analytical interest becomes data permission, delivery approval or a reporting delay.

lessons.title: Return a proposal that can be examined honestly
lessons.summary: Bring the baseline, target rationale, distribution and open questions together without inventing a later success.
lessons.objective: Summarize the practice baseline and target alternatives with their exact status.
objectives: Summarize the practice baseline and target alternatives with their exact status.
Identify the limitations and next considerations that belong in a useful recommendation.
Describe the actual change in Morgan and Nina’s proposal without claiming implementation or later benefit.
takeaways: A recommendation can be useful while important questions remain open.
State what changed in the proposal separately from what happened in actual work.
Missing later results mean unknown, not success or no warning signs.
lessons.statement: Return the supported comparison, why it matters and what remains to be considered.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands while the third stands between them.

intro.heading: Return a proposal that can be examined honestly
intro.body:
At the end of the original exercise, Morgan and Nina revise their proposal. It now identifies twenty-nine qualifying recorded replies among forty unique requests in one shared interval, 72.5 percent. It keeps North’s eighteen of twenty, 90 percent, and South’s eleven of twenty, 55 percent, with a thirty-five-percentage-point baseline gap. It describes the next-step communication event without renaming it understood instruction, correct advice or completed service. This clearer proposal is the supplied change; no actual DHS improvement or future observation is provided.

The possible target remains a planning illustration. Thirty-six qualifying replies out of the same hypothetical forty would be 90 percent, seven more events than the baseline. Morgan and Nina retain the two distributions: twenty in North and sixteen in South would mean 100 and 80 percent, while eighteen in each would mean 90 and 90. Their overall totals match but their gaps differ. The proposed target does not establish resources, approval, cause or useful next actions for people.

They also keep the sixteen-in-each illustration. It would yield 80 percent overall and zero gap while North falls ten percentage points and South rises twenty-five relative to the baseline. The purpose is to show why equal recorded levels alone do not describe every change. The recommendation does not automatically select the lowest gap or highest total. It asks which intended outcome, context, affected perspectives and capacity evidence would support a fitting real proposal.

Nina’s revised recommendation is to examine the defined reply step alongside its usefulness before adopting an actual target. It identifies missing evidence about correct and understood next action, the reason for the recorded distribution and the practical conditions for delivery. Morgan accepts those as considerations to bring to the appropriate roles. No new data collection, target approval, assignment or service repair follows in the supplied story. Staff keep responsibility for their work with consultant guidance and feedback rather than transferring every task to the consultant.

An eventual actual review would need appropriate observations and definitions to examine change. Different request volumes, repeat events or altered intervals could affect comparability. A proposed review should fit the real decision and evidence; this course sets no mandatory weekly dashboard, universal stopping rule or staff-retention period. If later results are absent, say they are not known. Neither the practice arithmetic nor a quiet chart supplies a reason to declare all is well.

Privately write a short return note containing the baseline, planning target and distributions, the reason the comparison matters, and its main open questions. You may use the job aid without producing a public report or live artifact. The separate garden encounter remains valid personal learning about progress meanings, not a cause of the queue gap. A faithful proposal and widened understanding are worthwhile results at their actual scope. Keep further evidence, actual decisions and later outcomes open until they are genuinely available.

flashcards.back: Morgan and Nina revise the proposal’s wording, comparisons and open considerations; no implemented improvement is supplied.
A readable baseline, proposed target, distribution comparison and remaining questions.
Hypothetical planning rather than approved commitment or observed result.
What fitting later evidence would help examine the defined event and useful outcome?

accordion.heading: Examine the comparison and its consequences

items.title: Return the baseline and alternatives together
items.body: Morgan’s revised note retains twenty-nine of forty and both queue levels before presenting thirty-six of forty as hypothetical. The twenty-and-sixteen and eighteen-and-eighteen allocations have the same total but different gaps. Keeping both prevents an overall target from hiding distribution. The equal sixteen-and-sixteen illustration adds the caution that zero gap can coexist with decline in one recorded level and unmeasured useful outcomes.

items.title: Make a recommendation without inventing authority
items.body: Nina recommends examining the communication step’s usefulness and the target’s rationale before adopting an actual target. Morgan accepts those open considerations for appropriate roles. This is a substantive proposal, not a claim that new data was collected or a decision was approved. Missing capacity and outcome evidence can be stated plainly while staff keep their work and consultant guidance supports it.

items.title: Keep a later review honest
items.body: No future observation is supplied. A review would need evidence fitting the real question and understandable counting rules. If later data has different bases, periods or events, those differences must be considered rather than mechanically using the course’s forty-request arithmetic. No fixed cadence or universal privacy threshold is created. Absent later figures remain unknown and cannot support an all-clear message.

tabs.heading: Compare the interpretation and the next consideration

tabs.label: The proposal becomes the implementation
tabs.body: Morgan publishes that the new 90 percent result is operational. The story supplies a revised proposal, not observed future work or approved capacity. Nina can return the target as planning, identify its reason and limitations and retain what needs actual consideration. This keeps the work useful while preventing an invented operational achievement from being attached to DHS.

tabs.label: The lowest gap becomes the whole recommendation
tabs.body: Nina chooses sixteen events in each queue because zero gap is simple to explain. Morgan restores the baseline and notes North’s decline and South’s increase, alongside the unresolved useful-next-action question. The arithmetic does not by itself choose the best real course of action. A fitting recommendation needs its purpose, relevant context, evidence and responsible decisions instead of one isolated number.

tabs.label: The note states the actual result and next consideration
tabs.body: Morgan and Nina return the clearer baseline, target illustrations, distributions and missing evidence. Nina recommends examining useful next actions and the rationale before adopting an actual target; Morgan accepts those considerations for appropriate roles. The supplied improvement is the quality of their proposal. No implemented measure, new collection or later benefit is claimed, and unknown results remain unknown.

check.question: What can be reported as the supplied result of the exercise?
check.correct: Morgan and Nina revised the proposal to retain the defined baseline, hypothetical alternatives and open considerations; no implemented target or later benefit is supplied.
wrong: The 90 percent target is now achieved in actual DHS work.
The zero-gap illustration proves every queue improved.
No later figures means there are no warning signs.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The actual proposal change is described separately from implementation and unknown later outcomes.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The planning illustration is not a future observation or actual DHS result. The sixteen-in-each illustration includes a North decline from the baseline. Missing later evidence is unknown, not reassurance.

sorting.heading: Keep evidence, proposals and outcomes distinct

items.text: The baseline wording now names a recorded reply carrying a stated next step.
The note compares both thirty-six-event distributions and their gaps.
What evidence would help assess useful next actions?
What real context and capacity would support a fitting target?
The target is implemented and achieved.
There are no warning signs because future data is absent.

lessons.next: Use the job aid for a faithful proposal or private reflection.

scenario.context: This example: Morgan and Nina finish a revised proposal with the accurate baseline, hypothetical target alternatives and open evidence questions. No implementation or later observation is supplied.
options: Announce a new operating target and successful service improvement.
Hide the baseline and future uncertainties to make the note sound decisive.
Describe the clearer proposal and appropriate next considerations while keeping approval, implementation and later outcomes open.
responses: The exercise provides neither operating approval nor a later useful-outcome observation.
A readable recommendation needs the evidence and uncertainty that matter to its actual purpose.
The note reports the supplied change and supports useful consideration without invented results.

lessons.transfer: Privately write a short return note with the baseline, target status, distribution comparison and main open considerations.

move.control: You can return a useful recommendation while honestly describing its evidence, status and next considerations.
move.failure: A proposal becomes an implemented success, or missing future evidence becomes an all-clear.
move.next: Privately write a short return note with the baseline, target status, distribution comparison and main open considerations.

jobAid.title: Set useful measures and explain proposed targets
jobAid.subtitle: Retain the event, base, distribution and purpose while keeping actual decisions and later results clear.
remember: A recorded process step is not automatically a useful outcome.
The same overall percentage can contain different levels and gaps.
A proposed target and a clearer proposal are not approval, implementation or later success.

sections.heading: Describe the starting condition
items: This example has forty unique requests, each counted once within the same interval. Twenty-nine have a recorded reply carrying a stated next step during it; eleven do not have that interval event recorded. Twenty-nine of forty is 72.5 percent.

The reply event does not establish receipt, understanding, correctness or resolved need. Earlier or later events remain unknown. Selecting only the twenty-nine qualifying-reply requests would answer a different question; it cannot establish improvement across forty.
In actual work, the counting unit, interval and base must fit the question. This exercise does not prescribe the same denominator for every measure.

sections.heading: Explain the target’s status and reason
items: A proposed 90 percent illustration would be thirty-six qualifying reply events out of the same hypothetical forty, seven more than the baseline. It is not an observation, approved commitment, capacity finding or verified help to seven more people.

Consider why the event matters, relevant evidence and affected perspectives, constraints, useful outcomes and actual responsible decisions. An attractive percentage supplies none of those by itself. No universal target or arbitrary deadline is created.
Keep the supplied baseline, proposed target and later observation separate. No later observation is supplied here.

sections.heading: Read the distribution beside the total
items: Baseline North is eighteen of twenty, 90 percent; South eleven of twenty, 55 percent. Total twenty-nine of forty is 72.5 percent and the gap is thirty-five percentage points. The queues are invented processing labels, not demographic categories or evidence of a cause.

Hypothetical twenty North plus sixteen South gives thirty-six of forty, 90 percent overall, with 100 and 80 percent levels and a twenty-point gap. Hypothetical eighteen in each gives the same total, 90 percent levels and zero gap. Neither allocation is a delivery plan or observed improvement.

Hypothetical sixteen in each gives thirty-two of forty, 80 percent overall and zero gap. Relative to the baseline North falls ten percentage points, South rises twenty-five and the total rises seven and a half. Zero gap alone hides this movement and does not establish useful outcomes.

sections.heading: Recognize personally offered meanings
items: In the separate garden encounter, Leta’s weaving-circle milestone expresses recognizable continued effort toward a whole; Hollis’s seasonal-care interval recognizes work before a visible result. These are selected personal meanings, not group rules.

Remy’s busywork and reluctance judgments widen. The revised invitation welcomes a meaningful step and a reason for its fitting interval without requiring biographies. Acceptance and a completed display remain unknown.
No progress marker, checklist frequency or personal narrative establishes commitment, an IDI orientation or a personnel rating. The personal encounter does not explain the practice queue gap.

sections.heading: Retain actual duties and authority
items: A measure proposal does not authorize collection, linkage, access, disclosure, new demographic fields or public release. Actual purpose, information arrangements and responsible roles remain; removing names or choosing a low count is not an automatic privacy certificate.

A target does not approve resources, staffing, expenditures, schedules, eligibility or operating changes. Staff carry their own equity work with the consultant’s program guidance, knowledge and feedback; daily duties and qualifying formal analyses keep their actual tools and roles.

In the separate disability-related allegation example, supervisor Jules immediately reports all protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or agency AAO and follows applicable agency procedures or the Affirmative Action Plan. No proof, finished chart, course, consensus, apology or consultant reply is a reporting condition. Assigned investigation and nonretaliation remain.
The descriptive queue gap is not itself the supplied allegation or proof of a protected-class cause. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters remain referred to the appropriate ADSA office.

sections.heading: Return a useful proposal without a false result
items: Morgan and Nina revise the baseline wording, distributions and open questions. Nina recommends examining the reply’s usefulness and the target’s rationale before adopting an actual target; Morgan accepts those considerations for appropriate roles. That clearer proposal is the supplied change.

No new data collection, target approval, implementation or later benefit is supplied. A fitting future review needs actual evidence and understandable comparisons; no universal cadence, stopping rule or retention period is added. Missing later results are unknown, not success or no warning signs.
Use the full example privately without a live project or public artifact.

sources.title: CDC: Program Evaluation Framework overview
sources.note: Collaborative, fair and useful evaluation connects the question, evidence and interpretation. The target in the example is a proposal, not a mandated percentage or completed outcome.

sources.title: U.S. Government Accountability Office: Assessing Data Reliability
sources.note: Accuracy, completeness and applicability matter for the intended purpose. The defined reply count and its unanswered useful-next-action question stay distinct.

sources.title: DHS: Content and writing guidelines
sources.note: A clear purpose and necessary information make the baseline, proposal and remaining questions understandable without enlarging an observed event.

sources.title: DHS Equity Policy
sources.note: Daily equity work and qualifying formal analysis retain their required tools and roles. Processing differences in an example do not establish systematic disparities or approve operational changes.

sources.title: Minnesota Statutes: Section 13.05
sources.note: Necessity, purpose limitations and accuracy and access safeguards for individual information remain relevant to actual work. A learning exercise gives no new data access or permission to disclose.

sources.title: Council of Europe: Developing intercultural competence through education
sources.note: Personally offered, context-specific meanings can widen an initial judgment and shape a changed response. The garden encounter does not establish a fixed group trait or a developmental rank.

sources.title: MMB Policy 1436: Harassment and Discrimination Prohibited
sources.note: Managers and supervisors immediately report all protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow applicable agency procedures or the Affirmative Action Plan. Assigned investigation and nonretaliation remain.
